blocks.content: Glaciers form in regions where annual snowfall exceeds melting. Over time, snow compacts into firn and eventually into dense glacial ice.
• Common in polar and high-altitude regions.

items: Understand how altitude and latitude influence the elevation of the snowline globally.
Identify the stages of ice compaction: Fresh Snow -> Firn/Névé -> Glacial Ice.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glacier formation begins in regions above the snowline where snow accumulation exceeds ablation.
The snowline marks the lower limit of perpetual snow and ice cover.
Pressure and compaction transform snow into granular firn and eventually into glacial ice over time.

blocks.content: Snowline is the lowest altitude where snow remains throughout the year. It varies with latitude.
